subject: fix(dashboard): every owner transport failure is a retryable 503
prompt: I run `hermes dashboard` as its own process while a gateway is serving the same Hermes home, so the dashboard forwards session edits such as archiving (`PATCH /api/sessions/{id}`) to that gateway. When the gateway can't be reached at that moment, the errors are inconsistent: if the gateway has just died and its port refuses the WebSocket connection, the dashboard answers 409 ('Gateway connection failed; no local fallback'); if the gateway restarted between the dashboard finding it and asking it for a ticket, the answer is a 400. Only a raw socket error gives the retryable `503 owner_unreachable`. The UI treats 409 and 400 as final, so the edit is lost instead of retried. Any failure to reach the gateway should come back as 503 `owner_unreachable` (without the dashboard falling back to writing the database itself), while refusals the gateway actually sends back (permission_denied, not_found, storage_unavailable, ...) keep their current status codes.

subject: fix: a build command that starts outside the update job is put in it instead of refused
prompt: On native Windows with Python installed from the Microsoft Store, `hermes update` fails every Node build step with the refusal 'the command would start outside the update job', so the update can never finish its builds. Nothing is actually misbehaving: Store Python is a packaged interpreter, and a program it starts from outside its package (such as the managed node) is created outside the update's job because that job permits breakaway. The build should run, still contained by the update job; only a build command that Windows really will not place in the job should keep being refused without ever running.

subject: fix(bot-screen): the RFB bridge forwards SetDesktopSize instead of dropping the viewer's stream
prompt: When I watch the agent's virtual desktop in the browser viewer (noVNC through Hermes's WebSocket bridge), the connection drops as soon as the viewer asks to resize the remote screen to fit its pane, which it does because Xvnc is started with `-AcceptSetDesktopSize`. The log shows `unknown RFB client message type 251` and the stream closes; the viewer reconnects and the same thing happens again. It happens whether or not the viewer holds the input lease. A resize request carries no input, so it should be passed through to Xvnc intact for every viewer, including when it arrives split across several WebSocket messages.

subject: fix(display): memory progress lines render operations[] batches
prompt: When the agent writes memory using the memory tool's current call shape (a `target` plus an `operations` list, e.g. `{"target": "memory", "operations": [{"action": "remove", "old_text": "port 8080"}, {"action": "add", "content": "a"}, ...]}`), the tool progress line shown in the CLI, in gateway chats, by the API server and in the TUI reads `memory ?` or an empty preview instead of saying what is being written. The older single-operation shape, with `action`/`content`/`old_text` at the top level, still renders properly, e.g. `-memory: "port 8080"` or `+user: "Name: Alice"`. A call that uses `operations` should render its first operation the same way, and when the batch holds more than one operation, append how many more there are, e.g. `-memory: "port 8080" (2 more)`. A one-operation batch should look exactly like the old single-operation line, in both the short preview and the full progress row.

subject: fix(model_switch): treat a fall-through to OpenRouter's default as "no custom endpoint configured"
prompt: My session is running on Anthropic (`https://api.anthropic.com` with my Anthropic key). My config has no `model.base_url`, but `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in my environment. When I switch the session's model with provider `custom` (e.g. `/model m2 --provider custom`, or when the per-turn config sync picks up `provider: custom`), the switch succeeds but the session now points at OpenRouter's default endpoint with my OpenRouter key, a host I never chose. When a custom endpoint is configured in `model.base_url`, switching to `custom` from another provider correctly uses that endpoint. But when no custom endpoint is configured, the switch should keep the session's current endpoint and API key (here `https://api.anthropic.com` and my Anthropic key) instead of falling through to OpenRouter.

subject: fix(compression): in-place compaction accounts for every row behind a merged user turn
prompt: One of my turns crashed before the model replied, so the session's stored history has that unanswered prompt followed directly by my next prompt: two user messages in a row, which Hermes joins into one turn when the history is reloaded. Later in the same session usage crosses the threshold and context compression runs in place, and the result is wrong on both surfaces. In a gateway session the two old prompts get re-sequenced after the turn that is currently running, and a message from the summarized part of the conversation vanishes from display and search. In a resumed CLI session, the oldest message kept after the summary is left marked as compacted beside its live copy, so recall and search return it twice. Expected: after compaction the joined prompt appears exactly once in the live conversation (the unanswered prompt, a blank line, then the next prompt), every assistant reply is still displayed, and each message carried past the summary is recalled exactly once.

subject: fix(cli): one-sentence reasoning is not repeated as its own summary title
prompt: In the classic CLI with the modern (glyph) layout and reasoning display on, the model's reasoning streams live and the block is closed with a dim `∴ Thought for Ns · <title>` line, where the title is the reasoning's first bold heading or first sentence. When the whole reasoning is a single sentence (for example `scripted reasoning about gamma zeta-reason`), that sentence is printed twice: once as it streams and again as the title on the `∴` line. Expected: one-sentence reasoning is shown only once, and the block still ends with the `∴ Thought for…` line, just without repeating the sentence. Reasoning that has a heading followed by more text should keep showing that heading as its title as before.

subject: fix(tui-gateway): register the readiness done-callback off the lock and give joiners a short grace
prompt: In Hermes Desktop, readiness sometimes never settles and the blocking onboarding overlay stays up. The Desktop polls the gateway's `setup.status` and `setup.runtime_check` RPCs from separate places at the same moment (at boot, and again when `setup.ready` is broadcast). When a second `setup.runtime_check` arrives while the first one's probe is still running, the gateway answers it at once with the retryable `readiness check still in progress; retrying next tick` error, even though the probe only reads config and finishes a few milliseconds later. With both of that consumer's checks errored, the onboarding gate treats readiness as unknown, i.e. not ready. Expected: an overlapping poll that arrives while a quick probe is running should wait briefly for it and return the same successful result the first caller gets. Only a probe that is genuinely slow should make an overlapping caller get the retryable error, so overlapping polls still can't tie up the gateway's request workers.

subject: fix(tools): avoid duplicate sandbox env type dispatch
prompt: With the terminal backend set to `singularity`, `daytona` or `vercel_sandbox`, the terminal tool can't create its environment at all: every command fails with `TypeError: _build_sandbox_env() got multiple values for argument 'env_type'`. The `local`, `docker` and `ssh` backends work fine. Expected: the sandbox backends start normally and are given the configured cwd, timeout and task id (plus the image for singularity and daytona). Backends supplied by plugins, which are looked up by backend name, should still receive that name and the image as they do now.

subject: fix(cli): /toolsets reads the gateway session's report
prompt: In the classic CLI attached to the shared gateway, `/toolsets` prints this CLI process's own tool registry: the MCP server toolsets and plugin toolsets loaded in the gateway are missing, and the toolsets marked as enabled are the ones from my launch flags rather than the ones this session actually has. The Ink TUI and Desktop already show the gateway session's report for `/toolsets`, and in the classic CLI other per-session commands such as `/personality` and `/cron` are already answered by the gateway. Expected: when the classic CLI is on the gateway, `/toolsets` should show the gateway session's report, printed exactly as the gateway lays it out (it is already formatted with its own indentation and box, so its lines should not be indented again). Without a gateway connection, the local report should still be shown.

subject: fix(distribution): refuse symlinked targets before the first write
prompt: I installed a profile from a distribution and later replaced its `skills/` directory with a symlink to a shared skills folder. After the distribution changed upstream, `hermes profile update <name>` fails with `... skills is a symlink; refusing to replace it`. Refusing is fine, and the shared folder behind the link is left alone, but by the time the refusal fires the update has already overwritten the profile's `SOUL.md`, `mcp.json` and `cron/` jobs with the new versions without recording the new version, so the profile is left half-updated and every retry fails the same way. Expected: if any location the update would write through is a symlink, the update should refuse before changing anything, leaving every file in the profile byte-for-byte as it was. It should also never write through a symlinked `.env.EXAMPLE` into whatever the link points at.

subject: fix(agent): keep marker-merged user rows addressable after alternation repair
prompt: In the TUI/Desktop, I switch models mid-session (Hermes records the model-switch notice in the history as a user-role message) and then send a prompt. Once the session's history has been reloaded, that prompt can no longer be edited and resent. The client sends `prompt.submit` with `truncate_before_row_id` set to my prompt's row id and `confirm_truncate: true`, and the gateway refuses with `target user message is no longer in session history`, so the text I typed is dropped. On reload the model-switch notice and my prompt are joined into a single user turn, and that turn is treated as the model-switch notice rather than as my prompt, so my prompt's row id no longer resolves. Expected: the joined turn stays an ordinary user turn that can be found by my prompt's own row id, so resending cuts the history right before the notice and prompt and submits the new turn. What the model receives should not change, and a plain prompt followed by a notice should keep working as it does today.
